newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Nineteen feared dead in South African mine accident.
newsitem.headline: Nineteen feared dead in South African mine accident.

text.p: Continuing mudslides forced rescuers to withdraw on Thursday from a diamond mine in South Africa's Free State province after recovering the bodies of four of 19 miners believed killed.

The accident happened late on Wednesday at Roberts Victor Diamond Mine, owned by Vancouver-listed Botswana Diamondfields Inc, near Dealesville, some 60 km (38 miles) west of the provincial capital Bloemfontein.

"The rescue teams have withdrawn and they won't resume today (Thursday) because it's too dangerous to continue the search. The mud is still flowing in," mine spokeswoman Marietjie van der Merwe told Reuters.
Officials said four bodies had been recovered. Mine manager Peter Smith said earlier there was no hope for the 15 missing miners.
"All people we could possibly rescue have been rescued... Nobody could live through (those) mud crushes," he said.
"For all practical purposes the whole mining operation has been cancelled, because of a possible inflow of mud into the mine," Smith said.

Police spokesman Solly Lesia said more than 30 miners were rescued but two were in serious condition. Seventeen people died in 1994 when a wall burst at a slimes dam at a gold mine at Virginia in Free State province.
